title: Persist tenant role navigation grants with tenant_id so they can be read back and survive re-editing
goal: rbacbind.InsertRoleMenus inserts into system_role_menu without tenant_id, so grants written from a tenant console land on tenant_id = 0 while loadRoleMenus reads under the tenant scope. The grants are therefore unreadable the moment they are saved, and re-saving an existing tenant role deletes the rows it then fails to rewrite, silently wiping navigation access. The contrast case proves the intended design: replaceRolePermissions already resolves the owning tenant through roleOwningTenantIDTx and writes TenantID, which is why page/action permission keys are correctly isolated while menu grants are not. This wave gives InsertRoleMenus the same tenant argument, backfills historical tenant_id = 0 rows, and adds the regression that a second edit does not lose grants.
findings: F3 (P0): InsertRoleMenus writes system_role_menu without tenant_id (insertRoleMenuSQL has no tenant column), while loadRoleMenus filters by tenant scope; tenant role navigation grants are unreadable, and updating an existing tenant role deletes them permanently.

out: Changing the menu tree contract or the role-menu payload shape
Touching system_role_permission, which is already tenant-correct

implementationNotes: InsertRoleMenus already takes a db handle; add tenantID as an explicit parameter rather than deriving it inside rbacbind, so the call site stays responsible for resolving the owning tenant exactly as replaceRolePermissions does.

The call site must resolve the tenant from the role row (roleOwningTenantIDTx), not from the request context: the two can differ for a platform administrator editing a tenant role, and the row must follow the role.
The backfill can be fully automatic because system_role_menu joins to system_role, whose tenant_id is authoritative. Unlike the data-scope backfill there is no ambiguity to defer.
Preserve the delete-then-insert semantics of replaceRoleMenus; the bug is the missing column, not the replace strategy.

runtimeEvidence: create a tenant role with menuIds, read it back, and confirm the same menuIds
edit the same role twice and confirm the grants survive the second save
SQL snapshot: no new system_role_menu row with tenant_id = 0 for a tenant role

humanGates: Approve the 000026 backfill running automatically: it rewrites tenant_id = 0 rows to the owning role's tenant, which is a data mutation on existing installs.
completionChecklist: replaceRoleMenus resolves the tenant from the role row
Menu grants read back identical after create and after a second edit
No new tenant_id = 0 row for tenant roles
